title: Pointed geometric affine charts and adic open-image comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [rem-dl-a1-conventions]. Let $X_0/k_0$ be a smooth scheme of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $W_0\subset X_0$ be an affine open of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow W_0$ be a dense open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its closed complement is a finite set of closed points [def-weil-closed-points]. For a closed point $s\in W_0\setminus U_0$, put $k'_0=\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field], a finite extension of $k_0$ [def-pc-field-extension], and choose its embedding into $k$. There is a smooth geometrically connected [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses] affine finite-type curve $V_0/k'_0$, an open immersion $V_0\hookrightarrow W_0\times_{k_0}k'_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and a $k'_0$-rational point $t\in V_0$ whose projection $h:V_0\to W_0$ sends $t$ to $s$ and induces an isomorphism $\kappa(s)\simeq\kappa(t)$. The map $h$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]; $U_V=U_0\times_{W_0}V_0$ is a dense geometrically connected open of $V_0$ with finite closed complement; write $j_V:U_V\hookrightarrow V_0$ and $h_U:U_V\to U_0$.
For any lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $G$ on $U_0$ [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], restriction of the iterated Weil datum defines $G_V=h_U^*G$ over $k'_0$. The actual adic ordinary/higher direct images [def-wf-middle-extension, def-weil-derived-direct-image] have natural comparison isomorphisms, with pullbacks as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom],
$$h^*R^rj_*G\simeq R^rj_{V,*}G_V\quad(r=0,1).$$
These commute with the connecting maps for short exact sequences in [lem-dl-a1-weil-open-image-delta]. On the fibres at compatible geometric points over $s$ and $t$, these give isomorphisms of local geometric-Frobenius modules [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], with $F_t=F_s$ and $q_t=q_s$. For every closed point $v\in U_V$ mapping to $u\in U_0$, the fibre of $G_V$ identifies with that of $G$ and its local Frobenius is $F_u^{[\kappa(v):\kappa(u)]}$; in particular punctually pure sheaves of weight $a$ pull back to punctually pure sheaves of weight $a$ [def-weil-punctual-weights]. The comparison for $r=0,1$ also holds when $h$ is an open immersion of finite-type open neighborhoods, and is compatible with successive restrictions.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open (restriction to localized sites); geometric chart: varieties.tex Tag 04KV, lemma-geometrically-connected-if-connected-and-point. The adic/Weil enhancement is the finite-coefficient-stage and constant-field version required by main-20261015 sk-p-dl-a1-exact.proof.md, sentence beginning “At a missing point, after shrinking”.

proof.text: Write $W_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. Density puts the generic point of each one-dimensional component in $U_0$. A strict specialization chain inside the complement, preceded by a component generic point, would have length at least two. Thus the reduced closed complement has dimension at most zero; [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] makes it finite over $k_0$. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), $L=\kappa(s)$ is a finite field extension of $k_0$. It is separable: every element of the finite field $L$ is a root of $T^{\#L}-T$, whose derivative is $-1$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale] makes $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ etale. Put $m=[L:k_0]$, so $\#L=q^m$.

source.place: Tag 01TB, lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points (closed-point residue fields); the finite-type zero-dimensional complement argument

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $W'_0=W_0\times_{k_0}L=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{k_0}L)$. The homomorphism $A\otimes L\to L$, $a\otimes b\mapsto a(s)b$, is surjective and is the identity on $L$. Its kernel defines an $L$-rational point $t'$ above $s$, with the prescribed residue-field map equal to the identity on $L$. The tensor algebra is of finite type over $L$, generated by $a_i\otimes1$ for any finite generating set $a_i$ of $A$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] it is smooth of relative dimension one; by [lem-sc-smooth-normal] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] it is normal and Noetherian. Apply [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product] to obtain $A\otimes L\cong\prod_i B_i$ with each $B_i$ a domain. A field-valued homomorphism sends exactly one of the factor idempotents to $1$. For that index $i$, take $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_i=D(e_i)\subset W'_0$, and let $t$ be $t'$ in this open. This open is also closed and affine, and $B_i$ is a finite-type quotient of $A\otimes L$. Its domain makes $V_0$ nonempty and connected.

source.place: Tag 04KV, construction of the connected rational-point neighborhood; normal-affine component decomposition as in properties.tex Tag 0357

proof.text: The open immersion $V_0\to W'_0$ is etale, and the projection $W'_0\to W_0$ is etale by base change of $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Their composite $h$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation, lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. The same permanence statements for smooth relative dimension show that $V_0/L$ is smooth of relative dimension one. Apply [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] to its rational point $t$: $V_0$ is geometrically connected. Since etale maps are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], every nonempty open of $V_0$ has nonempty open image meeting $U_0$; hence $U_V=h^{-1}(U_0)$ is dense. The complement is finite by the dimension-zero argument of step 1 and [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite]. This also proves $\kappa(t)=L=\kappa(s)$ with the specified identification.

We also need geometric connectedness of $U_V$, not just its density. Over the algebraic closure $k$ of $L$, $V=V_0\times_Lk$ is connected by step 3, is smooth of relative dimension one by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], and is Noetherian and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, lem-sc-smooth-normal]. Its finitely many irreducible components [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] cannot meet: on a normal affine neighborhood [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product] expresses the ring as a product of domains, so its components are disjoint. Thus each component is open and closed, and connectedness forces just one. The base change of the finite boundary is finite over $k$ (tensor its finite coordinate algebra with $k$), so has dimension zero and cannot exhaust the one-dimensional $V$. Its open complement $U$ is therefore nonempty and irreducible, hence connected. The algebraic-closure criterion [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure], applied over $L$ with the algebraically closed extension $k$, gives geometric connectedness of $U_V$ in the sense of [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses].

source.place: Tag 04KV and normality after smooth base change; nonempty opens of the resulting irreducible geometric curve

proof.text: Put $W=W_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $V=V_0\times_Lk$ using the chosen embedding $L\hookrightarrow k$. The geometric map $h:V\to W$ is the open immersion identifying $V$ with the corresponding open in $W'_0\times_Lk=W$. Let $g_W$ be geometric $q$-Frobenius and $g_V$ geometric $q^m$-Frobenius. Then $hg_V=g_W^mh$. For $(G,\theta)$ define the pulled-back Weil isomorphism to be $h_U^*(\theta^{[m]})$, preceded by the pullback-composition comparison, where $\theta^{[m]}=\theta\circ g_U^*\theta\circ\cdots\circ(g_U^{m-1})^*\theta$ as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace, def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. At each finite coefficient level, pulling back a local constant trivialization gives a local constant trivialization with the same module. Quotient transitions are preserved. Thus [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] makes this the lisse $G_V=h_U^*G$ with the asserted iterated datum.

source.place: The rational-point/constant-field chart reduction, with the Weil iterate made explicit

proof.text: Here is the comparison on the actual coefficient sites. For either the geometric open $h:V\hookrightarrow W$ above or an ordinary open restriction, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $W_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$, and likewise $U_{V,\mathrm{proet}}$ with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_V$. Under these identifications inverse image is slice restriction. The constant rings $(A_n)_W|_V$ identify with $(A_n)_V$. Completed coefficient rings identify too: restriction evaluates on the same objects, and limits of sheaves are computed objectwise, so $(\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W)|_V=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_V$. Module pullback is therefore restriction with the same ring action, with no additional tensor extension. It is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. In particular it commutes with kernels, images and cohomology of complexes.

source.place: Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact, and the slice restriction adjunction; proetale.tex Tag 09AE

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] to $j:U\hookrightarrow W$, presented on the small pro-etale sites by $T\mapsto T\times_WU$, and localize at $V\to W$. For every finite coefficient ring $A_n$, it gives the natural isomorphism $\beta_{K,n}:h^*Rj_{*,n}K\simeq Rj_{V,*,n}h_U^*K$. The coefficient map and the localized morphism are precisely those of [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism], not a different base-change map. In a K-injective model its evaluation on $T\to V$ is the fibre-product identity $I(T\times_WU)=I(T\times_VU_V)$. The same identity applies with the completed coefficient ring. This exhibits the comparison on complexes, so it preserves shifts and every morphism, including boundary morphisms. No properness or assertion that $Rj_*$ is concentrated in degree zero is used.

To compare this with the specified adic operations, take an integral representative $K$ and its strict reduction tower $K_n$. By [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison], its actual integral $Rj_*K$ is the completed-ring K-injective direct image and is canonically $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRj_{*,n}K_n$, with the specified quotient transitions. By [lem-sp-slice-restriction-strict-derived-limit] restriction commutes with this total derived limit as a functor on strict towers, including all projections. Thus applying restriction to the displayed tower yields the tower of step 7, not just unrelated isomorphisms of its individual terms. The same restriction/limit comparison applied to $K=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ identifies the integral pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] with restriction. The reconstruction equality here is the completeness comparison in [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] for $f=\mathrm{id}$. Consequently step 7 gives $\beta_K:h^*Rj_*K\simeq Rj_{V,*}h_U^*K$ for the actual integral operations, naturally on the full ambient completed-ring derived categories.

source.place: Tags 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), 0D6G; completed coefficient and strict tower specialization

proof.text: The maps and their inverses in steps 7–8 are linear and natural in $K$. Apply rationalization and then pass to a common finite coefficient-field stage as prescribed in [def-weil-derived-direct-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. This gives $\beta_G$ on $\Qlb$ objects and morphisms. It remains a comparison of the same functors: its finite-level section formula is unchanged after coefficient extension. Exact restriction from step 6 gives $h^*\mathcal H^r=\mathcal H^rh^*$, so taking $\mathcal H^r(\beta_G)$ gives the displayed comparison for $r=0,1$. The ordinary direct image is $R^0j_*$ by [lem-dl-a1-weil-open-image-delta]; we retain the genuine degree-one cohomology sheaf $R^1j_*$.

source.place: Tag 0D6G after the integral/rational/common-stage coefficient constructions

proof.text:
For a short exact sequence of the three lisse sheaves, work in the underlying constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. By [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4), its boundary $w:G_2\to G_1[1]$ is the unique one giving its distinguished triangle. Exact restriction is t-exact, and its termwise functor preserves cone triangles, also after rationalization and common-stage passage [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated, def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. It therefore carries $w$ to the boundary $w_V$ of the pulled-back exact sequence, by the same uniqueness. The natural, shift-compatible comparison of step 7, extended in steps 8–9, gives
$$\beta_{G_1}[1]\circ h^*Rj_*(w)=Rj_{V,*}(w_V)\circ\beta_{G_2}.$$
Taking degree zero and the canonical shift identification gives $\beta^1_{G_1}\,h^*\delta=\delta_V\,\beta^0_{G_2}$. These are exactly the connecting maps in [lem-dl-a1-weil-open-image-delta], obtained from the underlying coefficient triangle. No triangulated structure on the category of Weil pairs is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0152, short-exact-sequence cone boundary; naturality of the sectionwise comparison of Tag 0D6G

proof.text: The comparison also respects the iterated Weil data. Indeed the square $hg_V=g_W^mh$ sends an object $T\to V$ and its $q^m$-Frobenius pullback to the same fibre products on both sides of $I(T\times_WU)=I(T\times_VU_V)$. Applying this identity to $\theta^{[m]}$ gives $\beta_G\,h^*\theta_{Rj_*G}^{[m]}=\theta_{Rj_{V,*}G_V}\,g_V^*(\beta_G)$, with the pullback compositions of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition]. The equality holds before inverse limits and hence after the functorial tower and scalar constructions of steps 8–9. Taking point fibres uses the same composite geometric point $h\bar t=\bar s$; the two pullbacks are identified by that same composition theorem and its rational version in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Naturality of the point transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] then makes this a comparison of the local Frobenius operators of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].

source.place: Tag 0D6G, sectionwise comparison and naturality; local operators given by the specified iterated Weil datum

proof.text: Here is the degree normalization, including the point reparametrization. For a closed $v\in U_V$ mapping to $u\in U_0$, put $d=[\kappa(u):k_0]$, $d'=[\kappa(v):L]$ and $e=[\kappa(v):\kappa(u)]$. The image $u$ is closed by [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), since its residue field embeds in the finite field $\kappa(v)$. The field tower gives $md'=ed$. The $d'$-fold local iterate of $\theta^{[m]}$ is therefore $\theta^{[md']}=\theta^{[ed]}$. Its point return transport is the same product of $ed$ geometric-$q$ transports: [lem-trf-point-transport-composition] groups consecutive transports into blocks, and [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-realization] realizes these equalities integrally; rationalization preserves them. Grouping those $ed$ factors into $e$ blocks of length $d$ is exactly the definition of $F_u^e$ in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Thus the identified fibre has operator $F_v=F_u^e$. This calculation applies as well to the boundary direct-image fibres of step 11. At the chosen $t$ one has $d=m$, $d'=1$, $e=1$, giving $F_t=F_s$ and $q_t=\#L=q_s$.

source.place: Chart reduction at the missing point; the local Frobenius equality required to apply the weight gap

proof.text: For purity, use [p-linear-triangular] over the algebraically closed coefficient field $\Qlb$: in a basis adapted to its invariant flag, $F_u$ is triangular with diagonal eigenvalues $\alpha_i$, and $F_u^e$ is triangular with diagonal $\alpha_i^e$. Also $q_v=q_u^e$, by counting coordinates in the degree-$e$ extension of finite fields. If $G$ is punctually pure of weight $a$, then [def-weil-punctual-weights] gives $|\iota(\alpha_i^e)|=|\iota(\alpha_i)|^e=q_u^{ea/2}=q_v^{a/2}$, proving the asserted purity, with the zero fibre vacuous. Finally repeat steps 6–10 for any open immersion of finite-type neighborhoods. For two successive restrictions the section identifications both forget the same intermediate factor in $T\times_WU$; hence their composite equals the single restriction comparison. The ring actions, complexes, strict towers and coefficient-stage maps are the same, so this equality persists on $R^0,R^1$, on their connecting maps and on their local operators.
